primary_question: Where in the annual cycle do migratory birds absorb temporal delays, and what predicts when those delays persist to fitness-relevant stages?

corpus_rule.study_unit: population/cohort transition between two sequential annual-cycle timing events
eligible_designs: same individuals measured at both timing events
population/cohort data with a reported transition slope and explicit paired annual-cycle events
primary_effect_requires: both timing variables expressed in the same temporal units or convertible to days
unstandardized slope beta_AB with uncertainty OR individual-level data permitting estimation
clear temporal ordering A before B
transition biological class assignable without inspecting the slope
exclude: cross-sectional mean dates without within-study transition relationship
correlation only from the primary raw-slope synthesis
studies selected because they reported successful buffering

evidence_tiers.A: experimental perturbation or repeated-individual within-individual timing anomaly with individual identity controlled
evidence_tiers.B: same-cycle individual A/B timing observations, within-year centered or year-adjusted, raw individual data or unstandardized individual-level slope available
evidence_tiers.C: paired cohort/population aggregate timing effect without individual A/B observations

primary_estimand.name: timing_propagation_coefficient
centering_priority: raw dates only when year effects are absent or controlled
primary_estimand.forbidden: Do not convert repeatability or correlation coefficients into beta_AB.
interpretation_boundary: beta_AB is a descriptive conditional timing-propagation slope in days/day
observational beta_AB does not identify a causal fraction of imposed delay retained
1-beta_AB must not be labeled causal buffering capacity without Tier A evidence
persistent individual schedules, shared drivers, selection and measurement error can contribute to beta_AB
forbidden_language: causal fraction of delay retained from observational slope

primary_hypotheses.label: stationary-period buffering
primary_hypotheses.licensed_interpretation: Supported H1 means timing associations are attenuated more strongly across stationary than active transitions in the eligible corpus; causal delay absorption requires Tier A support or convergence.

primary_hypotheses.label: available-time hypothesis
primary_hypotheses.prediction: within stationary transitions, beta decreases as reported/derivable available interval duration increases

primary_priority: source-reported typical or mean stationary-period duration
moderator_definition.forbidden: focal individual's own B-A interval as predictor of the same effect, or unrelated species-average duration added after outcome inspection

secondary_hypotheses.label: fitness-relevant persistence
secondary_hypotheses.prediction: persistent delay reaching the last pre-breeding transition is associated with stronger reproductive timing or vital-rate consequences where those outcomes are reported

primary_model_plan.phylogeny: include if species count and taxonomic coverage support stable estimation

sensitivity: Tier A effects only where estimable
directly observed or high-resolution dates only
exclude SAME_SAMPLE_DERIVED duration moderator from H2
measurement-error sensitivity when timing uncertainty is available
novelty_boundary: No claim that buffering, reset points, carry-over effects, en-route compensation, or fitness costs are new.
No claim of first meta-analysis until systematic novelty search is complete.
V5 novelty is prospective quantitative synthesis of stage-to-stage day-for-day timing propagation and its moderators.

measurement_error_plan.risk: measurement error in event A attenuates beta_AB toward zero and can mimic stronger buffering
sensitivities: directly observed or high-resolution dates only
exclude preclassified low-information upstream dates where classification is possible without beta_AB
errors-in-variables or SIMEX-style sensitivity when event-date uncertainty is supplied

dependence_plan.shared_source_sample_group: required when multiple transitions use the same tracked individuals or source panel

triggers: too few Tier A/B effects in ACTIVE or STATIONARY classes for the declared comparison
primary corpus requires converting correlations, standardized coefficients or repeatabilities into beta_AB
effect uncertainty is unavailable for enough effects to support the declared multilevel synthesis
